title: The future of feedback: Motivating performance improvement through feedback
author: Jackie Gnepp
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfthjnj6
materials: Online surveys, four versions. Survey-GivNeg.mht Survey-GivPos.mht Survey-RecNeg.mht Survey-RecPos.mht

steps.title: Introduce the online survey
steps.instruction: Present the survey introduction to participants, ensuring the following details are communicated:

substeps.instruction: State that the survey is short and estimated to take about 10 minutes to complete.
Affirm that all responses will remain anonymous.
Indicate that only aggregate results will be reported and no individual answers will be shared.
Provide contact information (email address) for questions or problems.

steps.title: Randomize participants into groups
steps.instruction: Implement a self-randomization process to assign participants into four unidentified groups (Gave positive feedback, gave negative, received positive, received negative) based on the last two digits of their home phone number.

substeps.instruction: Instruct participants that questions are divided among different people to keep the survey short.
Ask participants to provide the real last two digits of their home phone number to ensure even distribution.
Provide four clickable number ranges that link to different survey versions: 00 to 24, 25 to 49, 50 to 74, and 75 to 99.
